Adaptyv is building an automated lab thats let AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.


ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll build out antibody developability at Adaptyv — the panel of assays that separates a nice binder from a manufacturable, stable, well-behaved therapeutic. Aggregation, thermostability, self-association, polyreactivity, solubility, viscosity, and chemical liabilities: you'll build the experimental stack that flags these early, and make it something customers can order as a product.

These assays exist today as a scattered, bespoke collection. Your job is to turn them into one coherent, automated, high-throughput developability assessment — and to connect the experimental data to in-silico prediction so the lab and the models reinforce each other. You'll develop the assays hands-on, work with lab automation to scale them, and work with the software and ML teams to model the data and make it useful for protein designers. You'll lead the science and stay at the bench.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build and validate a developability assessment panel hands-on: thermostability (DSF/nanoDSF), aggregation and self-association (SEC, HIC, AC-SINS, DLS), polyreactivity/nonspecificity, solubility, and chemical-liability assessment.

 - Turn that panel into a productized, high-throughput service customers can order against their antibody campaigns.

 - Partner with lab automation to scale and automate the assays for reproducible, fast turnaround.

 - Work with the software and ML teams to structure developability data and connect it to computational developability prediction.

 - Interpret results and advise customers on liabilities, risk, and what to engineer next.

 - Set the scientific standard for what developability data we trust and report.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Deep, hands-on experience assessing antibody developability — you know the assay panel cold and have used it to triage real antibody campaigns.

 - Applied industry experience. You've done this in an antibody discovery, engineering, or development setting where decisions and timelines were on the line — not primarily in an academic research project. This is the core requirement.

 - Strong grasp of what makes a biologic developable — the link between early biophysical signals and downstream manufacturability and stability.

 - Builder who moves fast. You want to stand up new capabilities and productize them, not run a fixed service.

 - Interdisciplinary. You collaborate naturally with automation engineers and with software/ML people, and you're excited about closing the loop between wet-lab data and predictive models.

 - Data fluency (scripting, working with structured datasets) is a strong plus.


DETAILS

 - Location: Lausanne, Switzerland (on-site)

 - Type: Full time

 - Start date: ASAP



Application deadline

We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

Binding (BLI/SPR), developability, biophysical, and functional assays all produce data at scale; your job is to make that data correct, comparable, and useful.

This sits at the intersection of three things: data quality (is this number real, or an artifact?), bioinformatics (linking experimental results back to sequence, structure, and protein design), and dataset building (turning foundry output into the kind of high-quality, benchmarkable data that frontier AI labs actually want). You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with the lab scientists who run the assays, the software team who own the pipelines, and the customers who train models on what we produce. This is a hands-on build role, not a management one.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the scientific logic of data quality across the foundry: define what "good data" looks like for each assay type — expected signal ranges, control thresholds, failure modes, edge cases — and turn it into automated checks.

 - Build anomaly detection and QC models that catch bad data the eye would miss: assay drift, instrument variability, plate effects, false passes and false fails — and distinguish real signal from noise statistically.

 - Work with the software and ML teams to specify, review, and improve the automated data pipelines that process instrument outputs, feeding back precise requirements for what to flag, auto-reject, or route to human review.

 - Connect experimental results back to the protein side — sequence, structure, and design — so wet-lab data and computational models reinforce each other.

 - Turn foundry output into structured, documented, benchmark-grade datasets that are a genuine asset for our customers and for training and evaluating protein-design models.

 - Apply real statistical rigor to multi-condition data at scale — thousands of samples across hundreds of simultaneous experiments — and make the results interpretable and comparable across runs.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Strong data science / bioinformatics background — you're fluent in Python (pandas, numpy, the scientific stack) and comfortable owning messy, real-world experimental data end to end.

 - Genuine biology grounding — you understand proteins, assays, and sequence/structure/function well enough to know what the data means, not just how to process it. You don't need to be a bench scientist, but you can't be biology-blind.

 - Statistical maturity — process control, anomaly detection, handling variability and batch effects; you can tell drift from noise and defend the call.

 - Prolific builder with the receipts to prove it. You've shipped a lot — pipelines, tools, models, datasets — and can point to concrete things you built end to end and put into real use, not prototypes that died in a notebook. You move fast, systematize what works, and have no patience for babysitting a fixed dashboard.

 - AI-native builder. It's 2026 — you build with coding agents like Claude Code as a default, and you have sharp judgment about what they produce.

 - Interdisciplinary by instinct. You're energized working across the lab bench, software, and ML, and you treat automation and data infrastructure as part of your job.

 - Bonus: experience with protein/sequence-structure data (bioinformatics tooling, structural data), ML on experimental data, or building datasets for model training and benchmarking.

Adaptyv is building an automated lab thats let AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Our lab produces binding data faster than any one person can look at it. Runs come off the Gators and the Carterra, go through our processing pipeline, and land in a review queue. Somebody with real judgment then has to decide: is this curve real? Is that a fit artifact or a genuine two-state binding event? Does this replicate get delivered, or does the sample get re-run? That person is you.

The second half of the job is talking to the customer about it. When a design team gets a plate back and three of their best predictions look like non-binders, they want to talk to someone who can explain why: reference subtraction, avidity, an off-rate at the edge of what the instrument resolves, or simply a bad protein. You'll be that person, on the call, sharing your screen, walking through sensorgrams.

This is a role for a scientist who is very good at kinetics and also likes people. If you like one but not the other, you'll be unhappy here.

We'd prefer you in Lausanne with us. A lot of the judgment in this job comes from being able to walk over to the instrument and ask what actually happened. But we're not going to lose the right person over it, so remote or hybrid works if you're clearly the one.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Review the binding data coming out of the lab. Every SPR and BLI run passes through our processing pipeline and then to human review, and you're the expert eye on the output. You decide what gets delivered, what gets flagged, and what gets re-run.

 - Judge the curves, not just the numbers. A clean-looking Kd on a bad fit is worse than no number at all. You know the difference between a real off-rate and a drifting baseline, and you can say why.

 - Review data from our other assays too: thermostability, expression, developability, enzyme activity. Binding is the core of the role but it isn't all of it.

 - Talk to customers about their results. Deliverable walkthroughs, follow-up questions, and the awkward conversation when the data doesn't say what they hoped. You explain what we measured, how confident we are, and what to do next.

 - Turn review into experimental design. When something needs a re-run, you decide what changes: orientation, regeneration, concentration series, or a switch from BLI to SPR for the sensitivity.

 - Analyze at the batch level, not just the sample level. With hundreds of results per experiment, you should be writing a script to find the pattern rather than clicking through a queue. Systematic drift, a bad reference channel, or a target lot behaving differently than the last one shows up in aggregate long before it shows up in any single curve.

 - Feed what you learn back into the pipeline. When you catch a case where automation passed something it shouldn't have, or failed something it shouldn't have, that becomes a concrete requirement for the software team.

 - Work closely with production (what actually happened in the lab), QC (systematic quality), and customer success (the relationship around the science).


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - MSc or PhD in biochemistry, biophysics, or a related field, plus 3+ years working hands-on with binding kinetics.

 - Deep SPR and BLI experience. Biacore, Carterra, Octet, Gator: the platform matters less than the fact that you've run these assays, troubleshot them, and interpreted a lot of data from them. You've seen enough sensorgrams to know immediately when one is lying to you.

 - Real fitting judgment. 1:1 vs. bivalent, when steady-state is appropriate and when it isn't, how mass transport and avidity distort a result. You can defend a Kd, or refuse to report one.

 - Strong data analysis skills. Python or R, enough to pull a few hundred results out of a database, fit them, plot them, and find the outliers. This role generates too much data to review by hand.

 - You use AI tools seriously. We run on Claude Code and similar tooling internally, and the people who get the most done here are the ones who reach for it by default: writing the analysis script, querying the database, building the one-off dashboard. You don't need to have done this before, but you need to want to. If your instinct is that real scientists do it by hand, this isn't the place.

 - A self-starter who works independently. Nobody is going to hand you a prioritized queue every morning. You'll figure out what matters most, go do it, and tell us what you found.

 - A fast learner. Our platform, our assays, and our software change constantly. You'll be handed unfamiliar tools and expected to be productive with them quickly.

 - Startup speed, not academic pace. Experiments ship to paying customers on deadlines. Getting a good answer this week beats a perfect one next quarter, and we'd rather flag an ambiguous result than sit on it.

 - Comfortable in front of customers. Many are PhD-level scientists at pharma companies and AI labs, and they will push back. You should enjoy that conversation rather than dread it.

 - Able to explain hard things simply. Some customers are biophysicists. Some are ML researchers who have never touched a pipette. You adjust without condescending to either.

 - Honest about uncertainty. When the data is ambiguous, you say so, to us and to the customer. We would much rather flag a weak result than ship a confident wrong one.

 - Familiarity with other biophysical or functional assays (DSF, HPLC, plate-based activity assays) is a plus.


WHY THIS ROLE IS INTERESTING

Most kinetics scientists spend their careers running a handful of assays very carefully. Here you'll see more binding data in a year than most people see in a decade, across a wide range of targets and design methods, including a lot of AI-designed proteins that nobody has ever characterized. You'll build pattern recognition that is genuinely rare, and you'll be the person customers call when they need to know what their data actually means.

Experience maintaining records, documentation, or administrative information would be considered an asset.
Familiarity with standard office software and digital collaboration tools.
Exposure to onboarding activities, user support, feedback collection, or the preparation of guidance materials would be an advantage.
Skills
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively in an international and multicultural environment.
Service-oriented mindset and ability to interact professionally with a diverse range of stakeholders.
Good organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks, maintain accurate records, and follow up on activities.
Strong attention to detail and ability to handle information, documentation, and data with accuracy and confidentiality.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and collaborative document management tools.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in General Administration, Customer Service (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is a general secondary education diploma.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

Join the ATLAS Data Acquisition (DAQ) team and contribute to the modernisation of one of the world's most advanced scientific computing networks. Working alongside experienced network engineers, you will gain hands-on experience in the deployment, testing, operation, and monitoring of a high-availability, multi-terabit-per-second network that underpins the ATLAS experiment, while helping to develop future-proof monitoring and alerting solutions in collaboration with experts across CERN and the LHC experiments.
Your responsibilities
Participate in the installation, commissioning, testing, and operation of network infrastructure supporting the ATLAS Data Acquisition (DAQ) system.
Deploy and maintain a production-ready network monitoring and alerting solution for critical DAQ services and equipment.
Collaborate with experts from other LHC experiments to identify common requirements and contribute to the development of scalable, future-proof monitoring solutions.
Support the operation and upkeep of the ATLAS TDAQ laboratory, including infrastructure, equipment, and resource management activities.
Contribute to the maintenance and evolution of the ATLAS DAQ hardware infrastructure, including server deployment, hardware interventions, and related technical support.
Your profile
Basic experience as Sysadmin or Netadmin.
Hands-on experience with server and/or switch installations in professional environment.
Skills
Basic knowledge of TCP/IP stack and Ethernet networks.
Basic programming skills in Python and Bash.
General knowledge of Linux systems.
Ability to work in teams.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in Computing Infrastructures (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is a general secondary education diploma.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.
Applicants with a Bachelor's, Master's or PhD degree are not eligible.

À la Clinique de Crans-Montana, nous vous offrons l'opportunité de débuter votre parcours professionnel dans un environnement stimulant, humain et riche en découvertes.
Durant votre année de stage MPE, vous évoluez au sein de plusieurs secteurs administratifs essentiels au bon fonctionnement de l'institution, notamment la réception, les admissions, les ressources humaines, la gestion administrative et comptable ainsi que le secrétariat.
Accompagné ou accompagnée par des professionnelles et professionnels expérimentés, vous développez progressivement vos compétences en participant à des activités variées telles que la gestion de la correspondance, le suivi administratif des patientes et patients, l'élaboration de statistiques, la gestion des caisses et des fournisseurs, ainsi que la saisie d'écritures comptables.
La diversité des missions confiées et les exigences propres au milieu hospitalier vous permettent d'acquérir une expérience complète et enrichissante. Vous découvrez les multiples facettes du travail administratif tout en contribuant, à votre niveau, à la qualité de l'accueil et des prestations offertes à nos patientes et patients.
Cette année de stage constitue une excellente opportunité de mettre en pratique les connaissances acquises à l'école tout en développant de nouvelles compétences professionnelles dans un cadre formateur et valorisant.

Within the FAP Department, you will join the Business Computing (BC) Quality and Service Team and contribute to delivering high-quality IT services across the organisation. You will play a key role in providing second-line support for business applications, coordinating hardware support activities, assisting users, and helping improve service processes through automation and documentation.
This position offers a unique opportunity to work in a diverse IT environment, collaborate with experts across multiple domains, and gain hands-on experience in IT support, service management, hardware lifecycle management, and process improvement.
Your responsibilities:
User Support & Service Delivery
Provide second-line support for Business Computing applications, investigating and resolving user issues.
Deliver technical assistance and guidance to users of Business Computing services and applications.
Coordinate with application experts, IT specialists, service providers, and support teams to ensure timely resolution of incidents and service requests.
Hardware & Asset Management
Provide hardware-related support to designated users and coordinate equipment interventions, office moves, and replacements.
Manage computer equipment inventory, stock levels, asset tracking, and associated administrative processes.
Documentation & Knowledge Management
Create, maintain, and enhance technical documentation, software installation guides, knowledge base articles, and operational procedures for the team and Service Desk.
Operational Improvement & Security Coordination
Contribute to IT security activities by liaising with security experts and promoting good security practices.
Identify and implement opportunities to streamline and automate operational and administrative processes.
Your profile:
Experience in one or more of the following areas would be considered an advantage:
Windows and Mac workstation administration and troubleshooting.
Hardware deployment, inventory management, or asset management.
IT support, help desk, service desk, or technical user support.
Experience with ServiceNow.
Technical documentation and knowledge management.
IT service management practices and ticketing systems.
Skills:
Interest in IT support, technology, and helping users.
Basic understanding of computer systems, hardware, networking, and cybersecurity.
Strong problem-solving and communication skills.
Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment.
Organised, reliable, and eager to learn.
Interest in improving processes and finding efficient ways of working.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in Computer Science / Computer Engineering (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is either a Bachelor's or Master's degree.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.
Applicants without University degree are not eligible.
Applicants with a PhD are not eligible.

Introduction:
The CERN Staff Association (SA) is committed to promoting the welfare of CERN personnel through a wide range of services and initiatives. Among these is the Jardin des Particules (JDP), an early childhood education and childcare facility located at CERN, welcoming children from 4 months to 10 years old.
We are looking for an experienced Administrative Assistant to play a central role in the day-to-day administration and management of the Jardin des Particules. This is a varied position combining human resources administration, financial management and operational coordination within a Swiss employment framework.
If you enjoy taking ownership of diverse administrative responsibilities, have solid knowledge of Swiss employment administration and thrive in an international environment, then join the CERN Staff Association and contribute to an essential service for the CERN community.
Functions:
As an Administrative Assistant in the CERN Staff Association, you will report directly to the Presidents of the Staff Association and work closely with the Management Committee of the Jardin des Particules, external service providers and the Staff Association Secretariat.
Your primary responsibility will be to ensure the efficient administrative, human resources and financial management of the Jardin des Particules.
Your main responsibilities will include:
Managing the full administrative lifecycle of JDP employees, including recruitment administration, employment contracts, amendments, onboarding and departures.
Coordinating payroll administration with the external fiduciary and ensuring the accuracy of salary-related information.
Managing personnel administration in accordance with Swiss employment legislation, including social insurance, pension schemes (LPP), employment contracts, leave management and other statutory obligations.
Acting as the main administrative contact for JDP staff on employment-related matters.
Monitoring the JDP budget, processing invoices and payments, maintaining accounting records and supporting financial reporting.
Performing financial monitoring and analysis to support sound budget management.
Liaising with external partners including the fiduciary, insurance providers and public authorities when required.
Preparing communication and promotional material for the Jardin des Particules and supporting its visibility within the CERN community.
Contributing to the continuous improvement of administrative and financial processes.
In addition, you will provide occasional support to the Staff Association Secretariat by welcoming visitors and responding to general enquiries.

Vous intervenez dans le cadre de missions de remplacement de courte à moyenne durée au sein de différents secrétariats médicaux. Ce poste s’adresse à des personnes appréciant la diversité des environnements de travail, le rythme soutenu et la capacité à s’adapter rapidement à de nouveaux contextes professionnels. Le principal défi de cette fonction réside dans la variété des activités et la durée limitée des missions, ce qui requiert une excellente capacité d’apprentissage, d’analyse et d’écoute.
Grâce à votre aisance relationnelle, vous assurez l’accueil, l’information et l’orientation des patientes et patients se présentant dans le service, tout en gérant efficacement les appels téléphoniques entrants. Vous participez activement à l’organisation des consultations en administrant les agendas électroniques des médecins et en préparant les dossiers patients. À l’issue des consultations, vous assurez de manière autonome, rapide et rigoureuse la frappe des rapports médicaux et, lorsque cela s’avère nécessaire, vous planifiez les examens médicaux complémentaires.
Parallèlement, vous prenez en charge l’ensemble des activités administratives liées au fonctionnement du secrétariat. Cela comprend notamment le suivi des dossiers patients, la gestion du courrier et de la messagerie électronique, l’actualisation des plannings ainsi que, le cas échéant, l’organisation de congrès ou d’événements du corps médical. Vous faites preuve de proactivité dans l’accomplissement des tâches logistiques inhérentes à la vie d’un secrétariat, telles que les commandes, les notes d’honoraires et l’archivage.
Au sein des équipes, vous développez des relations de travail basées sur la collaboration et la confiance avec les autres secrétaires médicales et médicaux. Vous contribuez à assurer la continuité du service lors des absences et acceptez d’évoluer au sein de bureaux partagés. Plus largement, votre sens du service et votre agilité vous permettent de mettre votre polyvalence au profit de l’institution et d’intervenir dans différents services en fonction des besoins.
Doté ou dotée d’un bon sens de l’organisation et d’une gestion efficace des priorités, vous êtes reconnue ou reconnu pour votre autonomie, votre rigueur et votre précision dans l’exécution des tâches qui vous sont confiées. Vous savez également faire face aux imprévus avec sang-froid et gérer les situations de stress de manière constructive.

En tant qu’aide en soins et accompagnement, vous prenez en charge des patients et patientes de tout âge. Sous la responsabilité du personnel infirmier, vous effectuez des soins de base et d’accompagnement en leur apportant un soutien constant, tout en développant et favorisant les relations humaines. 
Vous participez également à l’organisation d’activités quotidiennes permettant d’assurer leur bien-être physique, psychique et social. Vous apportez ainsi soutien et suppléance dans les activités de la vie quotidienne des patientes et patients et dans l’accompagnement de leur famille. 
Vous assurez les tâches de propreté de l'environnement proche du patient ou de la patiente et vous contribuez à sa sécurité en respectant les règles d'hygiène et d'asepsie en vigueur. 
Vous participez activement à la prévention de complications liées à l’hospitalisation en collaboration avec les autres corps professionnels de santé (douleur, prévention escarre, prévention chute…).

Work with us to evolve the CERN data storage systems used at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) and at its international partners. CERN is the birthplace of the World Wide Web and one of the world’s leading laboratories for particle physics. Join the Storage and Data Management Group in CERN’s IT Department as a Distributed Storage Engineer for a unique challenge as the next step in your career. CERN, take part! The CERN IT Storage and Data Management group operates the core services used by both LHC and non-LHC experiments for data collection, archival, reconstruction, analysis, and global distribution via the Worldwide LHC Computing Grid. Join us to work on core data storage and management capabilities which enable scientific progress at CERN!
As a Distributed Storage Engineer, you will contribute to the design, evolution, and operation of large-scale, distributed critical storage services for the CERN cloud and computing infrastructures. You will join a team to work with open-source Ceph-based block, object, and filesystem solutions (including CephFS and NFS integrations), ensuring high availability, performance, and resilience across multi-datacenter environments.
Your role will involve system-wide troubleshooting in a distributed Linux-based environment and optimising storage architectures for demanding workloads. You will use your C++ software development skills to help identify and troubleshoot issues with the Ceph code base and to contribute code improvements to the upstream open-source Ceph project when necessary.
You will have opportunities to learn and contribute to improving automation, deployment, and observability, aligned with modern DevOps practices, to participate in inspiring projects and new technologies such as storage for HPC and AI/ML and to engage with our international partners, participating to conferences and workshops.
Functions
Management and operations of distributed disk storage, block, object and filesystem services based on mainstream open-source technologies (Ceph)
Participate in the evolution of architecture and design of storage services for CERN and software-defined storage technology with Open Source
Integrate, troubleshoot and maintain distributed disk storage systems at scale, across multiple availability zones and data centres.
Contribute to documentation, development, optimisation and further automation of storage services.
Contribute to change management, incident response, and user support.
Liaise with key stakeholders inside and outside of the IT department.

The SY-BI group in CERN's Accelerator Systems Department develops and operates the instruments used to observe particle beams and measure their key properties. These systems are essential to the reliable operation, optimisation, and future development of CERN's accelerator complex.
You will contribute to the development of next-generation beam-position monitoring systems for CERN's injector complex, including the pre-accelerators and Antimatter Decelerator. You will work on innovative high-speed data-acquisition platforms combining fast digitisers with advanced System-on-Chip (SoC) technologies.
This role offers a hands-on opportunity to work at the intersection of digital electronics, embedded systems, real-time signal processing, and accelerator physics. It is particularly suited to people with an interest in FPGA or HDL development, high-speed electronics, embedded software, digital signal processing, instrumentation, or experimental physics.
Your responsibilities:
Develop, integrate and test FPGA gateware and embedded SoC firmware for a SoC device.
Implement data acquisition and data processing logic and real-time digital signal-processing algorithms.
Validate system performance in laboratory and accelerator environments.
Perform data analysis in Python.
Assist measurement campaigns in the accelerator complex.
Collaborate with experienced engineers, physicists, and technicians from different teams across CERN.
Your profile:
Experience in digital signal processing.
Demonstrated experience with FPGA and SoC.
Experience in Software programming (e.g. Python, C++).
Demonstrated experience with Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC and/or RFSoC would be an advantage.
Skills:
Knowledge of Verilog and SystemVerilog.
Knowledge of digital electronics.
Knowledge of Python.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
You have a professional background in Electronic Engineering (or a related field) and have either:
a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;
or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

Help shape the future of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) machine protection systems. We are looking for a motivated Engineer to contribute to the renovation of the LHC Collimator Control System, a critical component ensuring the safe and reliable operation of the world's most powerful particle accelerator. Working in a highly collaborative environment you will help to increase the reliability, usability, and long-term maintainability of systems at the heart of LHC operations. This is a unique opportunity to combine software development, controls engineering, and accelerator technology while making a tangible impact on CERN's flagship facility.
Your responsibilities
Develop and maintain control applications for the LHC Collimator system using the FESA framework, ensuring integration within CERN's accelerator control environment.
Coordinate and support control system commissioning, performing functional testing, validation, and verification of interlocks and fail-safes prior to operational deployment.
Integrate control systems with the alarm server and develop high-level tools to enhance usability and real-time monitoring.
Contribute to the design and validation of system-level tests, including functional, integration, and regression testing.
Support expert and operational interfaces, providing diagnostic capabilities and improving intervention workflows.
Your profile
Demonstrated experience in real-time or distributed control systems, preferably within accelerator, industrial automation, or scientific environments.
Experience in interventions in complex industrial or technical environments.
Experience developing and maintaining expert interfaces (GUIs, web tools) for control and diagnostics.
Experience with software version control (e.g. Git) and CI/CD workflows.
Skills
Proficiency in C++.
Knowledge of Python.
Skilled in system integration, commissioning, and validation of control applications for hardware-software systems.
Strong ability to troubleshoot, analyse, and document complex technical issues in operational environments.
Proactive, organised, and collaborative, with the ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary engineering teams and communicate technical progress clearly.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
You have a professional background in Controls Engineering, Computer Science, Electronic Engineering (or a related field) and have either:
a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;
or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

Le CERN est un centre de recherche en physique des particules, il accueille des scientifiques du monde entier. Le Service d’Information Scientifique du CERN offre un environnement de travail dynamique, international et stimulant.
Pour la rentrée 2027, nous sommes à la recherche d'un(e) apprenti(e) motivé(e) pour apprendre le métier d'Agent en Information Documentaire dans un environnement scientifique et multilingue.

Intégrez et renforcez une équipe composée de 2 développeurs fullstack et un lead développeur, dont la mission est de poursuivre le développement et l’évolution de l’application Greco, le logiciel de gestion de planning et de téléconsultation utilisé par le personnel. Le logiciel est également utilisé par les patients et patientes grâce à l’application Concerto. L’équipe travaille de manière agile en s’inspirant fortement de la méthodologie Scrum tout en s’adaptant aux contraintes liées au milieu hospitalier qui impliquent d’être capable de parfois devoir changer rapidement de tâche pour s’adapter aux priorités. 
Vous participez à la rédaction des cahiers des charges techniques, en traduisant les besoins fonctionnels en spécifications détaillées. À partir des spécifications techniques, vous développez le logiciel, aussi bien sur la partie front-end que back-end, en utilisant les technologies de pointe et une architecture microservices. Vous faites évoluer la solution et garantissez sa maintenance, tout en assurant un suivi rigoureux. Concrètement, vous développez en autonomie les fonctionnalités et corrections qui vous sont attribuées. 
Grâce à votre esprit d’équipe, vous collaborez étroitement avec l’équipe pour développer des solutions et des fonctionnalités fiables et évolutives.  Vous partagez les meilleures pratiques et adoptez une approche critique et constructive dans une optique d’amélioration continue en faisant preuve d’une forte orientation solution. 
Tout au long du cycle de vie du produit, grâce à votre sens de la communication, vous contribuez au développement du logiciel de manière optimale et structurée, assurant un lien essentiel avec les coordinateurs et coordinatrices greco des différents départements médicaux. Vous adaptez votre langage en fonction de vos interlocuteurs et interlocutrices pour vulgariser les termes techniques, challengez les solutions proposées, et collaborez activement avec les parties prenantes pour trouver les adaptations les plus pertinentes. 
De plus, vous veillez à la mise à jour et à la rédaction de la documentation nécessaire. Vous mettez à profit votre capacité de synthèse et votre pragmatisme pour mener votre mission dans les délais impartis et garantir un résultat de qualité. 
Vous participez activement à l’ensemble des phases d'un projet informatique, de son initialisation à sa finalisation, en vous assurant de produire les livrables attendus à chacune de ces phases. En outre, vous assurez également le support utilisateurs de niveau 3, en relation avec les autres services de la DTN-IA, tout en assurant une orientation client forte.

Au cœur du parcours patient, vous assurez les transports des patientes et patients au sein de l’institution, en veillant à leur confort ainsi que leur sécurité dans le respect des normes d’hygiène et des délais impartis.
Ce rôle intègre une dimension humaine importante dans l’accompagnement du patient. Votre sens de l’écoute et votre bienveillance, vous permettent d’instaurer un climat de confiance. Chaque trajet devient ainsi une prise en charge individualisée grâce à vos qualités relationnelles. 
Vous intervenez également dans le transport urgent de matériel médical, de produits pharmaceutiques et de prélèvements de produits biologiques et sanguins. Vous vérifiez avec rigueur à leur bon conditionnement ainsi qu’à la conformité des informations des données d’identification.
Votre adaptabilité et votre aptitude à collaborer avec des équipes pluridisciplinaires permettent d’assurer une coordination fluide des activités et un haut niveau de qualité, y compris en situation imprévue.
Par votre engagement, votre sens du service et votre empathie, vous participez concrètement à assurer des prestations de qualité dans un environnement hospitalier serein, sécurisé et centré sur le bien-être des patients.

In preparation for the High-Luminosity LHC phase, the CMS collaboration is working on an ambitious upgrade of the first stage of its online selection system, the Level-1 (L1) trigger. The upgraded system will use powerful FPGA processors connected through a high-bandwidth network, paving the way for more sophisticated online algorithms such as Particle Flow reconstruction.
By joining the team, you will contribute to the development of these algorithms, their implementation in firmware, and the evaluation of their physics performance.
Your responsibilities:
Contribute to the development of algorithms for the CMS Level-1 (L1) trigger.
Integrate and maintain contributions from other developers to support collaborative project development.
Evaluate the physics performance of the algorithms and contribute to the development of monitoring systems.
Participate in the hardware testing and installation of the upgraded trigger system.
Collaborate closely with members of the CMS L1 trigger groups at CERN.
Present project progress and results at collaboration meetings, workshops, and international conferences.
This role includes team supervision responsibilities.
Your profile:
Experience in FPGA firmware development using HDL and High-Level Synthesis (HLS) tools.
Experience in data analysis, preferably in the field of high-energy physics.
Practical experience in developing and applying machine learning solutions to real-world problems.
Experience with Continuous Integration (CI) and quality assurance techniques and tools.
Familiarity with trigger or data acquisition systems and their associated hardware, such as high-speed optical links, would be an advantage.
Skills:
Proficiency in software development using C++, Python, and Git is required.
Knowledge of data analysis tools and techniques, including ROOT and machine learning frameworks, is required.
Experience with the following software and technologies would be an advantage: Vivado Design Suite, Vivado/Vitis High-Level Synthesis (HLS), GitLab, and continuous integration workflows.
Strong collaborative skills and effective communication are essential.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
You have a professional background in Physics (or a related field) and have either:

Translate client business questions into appropriate research approaches and structured project plans
Conduct primary research, including interviews with physicians and other healthcare professionals in German and, where appropriate, French
Complement primary research with targeted secondary research and desk analysis where required
Analyze and synthesize market, competitor, and stakeholder evidence to identify relevant insights, opportunities, and risks
Translate complex findings into clear, actionable commercial recommendations and compelling client storylines
Prepare high-quality reports and presentations and deliver results to client stakeholders
Own project timelines, deliverables, and day-to-day client interactions across the full project lifecycle
Manage several projects in parallel while collaborating effectively with colleagues across teams and disciplines
Contribute to the continuous development of research approaches, client solutions, and team capabilities

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree, ideally in life sciences or a related field
2–5 years of relevant professional experience in pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, healthcare consulting, market research, competitive intelligence, or a related field

Strong analytical skills, with the ability to synthesize complex evidence into business-relevant insights
Excellent communication and presentation skills, with a confident and client-oriented approach

The role reports to the Team Lead Qualitative Insights within the Primary Market Research Team of the Swiss Analytics & Advisory Services Team.

The Engineering Department (EN) pushes the boundaries of technology to enable physicists to carry out world-class scientific research. Within the EN Department, the Cooling and Ventilation Group (EN-CV) is responsible for the design, construction, operation, and maintenance of the cooling and ventilation installations that support CERN's accelerators, experimental facilities, and technical infrastructure.
Within EN-CV, the Controls Section (EN-CV-CL) is responsible for the specification, development, commissioning, operation, and maintenance of the industrial control systems used across all EN-CV installations.
The EN-CV control systems are based on industrial technologies, including Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems, the UNICOS framework developed at CERN, automated code generation tools, and virtual commissioning methodologies. More than 650 PLCs are currently deployed and operated across EN-CV facilities, requiring a very high level of reliability, availability, and maintainability.
As a Controls Engineer, you will be involved in the full lifecycle of industrial control systems, from defining requirements and technical specifications to designing and implementing control solutions.
Functions:
Define control system requirements and produce functional specifications for cooling and ventilation installations.
Select and apply appropriate control and automation strategies to meet operational, reliability, and energy efficiency objectives.
Design, develop, test, and validate PLC application software for cooling and ventilation installations, ensuring compliance with applicable EN-CV-CL standard solutions and CERN UNICOS framework.

Dans ce cadre, vous participez également activement à l’actualisation de la documentation qualité au sein de la GED biomédicale.
Le réseau biomédical de suisse romande est organisé autour de 3 Groupes Techniques biomédicaux romands (investissements et veille technologique, maintenance et exploitation, qualité et vigilance), vous participez activement au développement de ce réseau en reprenant les avancées des différents travaux effectués par ces GT et consolidez les travaux à venir (benchmarks et comparaison entre hôpitaux et cliniques), créez des standards et mettez à disposition l’information à travers des outils de communication à construire et à alimenter. Dans ce cadre, vous êtes amenée ou amené à travailler et échanger avec tous les services biomédicaux hospitaliers de Suisse romande.
Vous avez par ailleurs l’opportunité de vous impliquer concrètement dans plusieurs projets à différents niveaux d’avancements ou de coordination.

En tant qu’ingénieur ou ingénieure cheffe ou chef de projet, vous renforcez le secteur ingénierie et techniques du bâtiment (SITB). L’équipe, composée d’une dizaine de personnes spécialisées dans les différents domaines techniques du bâtiment : Chauffage-Ventilation-Climatisation (CVC), sanitaire, gaz médicaux et électricité, gère environ 60 projets en parallèle. Vous évoluez ainsi dans un environnement à la fois exigeant et innovant.
Dans ce rôle, vous pilotez des projets de construction ou de rénovation, depuis leur conception jusqu’à leur réalisation, tout en mettant en avant vos expertises en CVC, Sanitaire, Gaz Médicaux et Régulation. Concernant le CVC, vous intervenez sur des installations comme les centrales de traitement d’air, la production et la distribution de chauffage, d’eau surchauffée, de vapeur et d’eau glacée. Pour le sanitaire, vous travaillez sur des projets liés à la production et à la distribution d’eau chaude sanitaire, d’eau purifiée ou refroidie.
Vous réalisez des études avant-projets en analysant la faisabilité, en identifiant les besoins, en estimant les coûts et en définissant le planning. Vous rédigez des cahiers des charges détaillés et proposez des solutions techniques qui permettent une prise de décision éclairée. Vous assurez un cadrage rigoureux des projets, garantissant ainsi une validation précise des objectifs et un déroulement maîtrisé.
Vous évaluez les solutions techniques en sélectionnant les équipements les plus adaptés et en élaborant des plans détaillés. Vous préparez également les soumissions nécessaires pour le lancement des appels d’offres publics. Vous assurez une supervision active en veillant au respect des lois, des normes et des réglementations en vigueur à chaque étape.
Vous supervisez l’exécution des projets en coordonnant les différentes étapes, en suivant le budget et le planning, et en assurant une collaboration optimale avec les équipes projets. Vous participez aux comités de pilotage (COPIL), où vous présentez l’avancement des travaux, proposez des solutions aux éventuels défis et contribuez aux prises de décisions stratégiques.
En collaboration avec vos collègues, vous intervenez sur d’autres projets transverses pour coordonner les actions, résoudre les problématiques et proposer des solutions adaptées. Vous partagez également votre expertise avec vos pairs pour les accompagner dans la gestion de leurs propres projets.
Dans une perspective transverse, vous participez activement à l’amélioration continue en contribuant à l’évolution des référentiels et des directives techniques. Vous mettez à jour la documentation, effectuez une veille technologique dans vos domaines d’expertise et proposez des améliorations pertinentes.

Vous êtes intégré ou intégrée dans le service biomédical et équipements des HUG, au sein du Secteur d’Ingénierie Biomédicale (SIB), et êtes encadrée ou encadré par d’excellents et excellentes professionnelles.
Ce stage s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet majeur de construction du nouvel hôpital des enfants qui sera livré en 2035. Vous assistez l’ingénieur biomédical en charge de ce projet, en collaboration avec les référents techniques, les utilisateurs et les fournisseurs. Vous contribuez à la démarche de veille technologique visant à identifier les solutions techniques nouvelles et/ou innovantes, leurs bénéfices et les contraintes afférentes.
Le travail et sujet principal du stage concernent l’actualisation d’un plan d’équipement hospitalier complet selon derniers plans et numération des locaux, la mise à jour des réservations techniques et des contraintes d’implantation des matériels (selon les standards et veille technologique), ainsi que l’analyse des charges liées attendues (liées à l’installation des matériels leurs connectivité et maintenance). De plus, une analyse et actualisation du parc d’équipements actuels de la pédiatrie HUG par unités et catégories (valorisation, histogramme, maintenance) permettra une projection des coûts d’investissements et de transferts selon les scenarii calendaires de fin de projet et identification des enjeux.
Vous vous impliquez dans la préparation d’une rocade préparatoire au projet concernant l’imagerie radiologique (fiches locaux et plans ; imagerie CT IRM RX, anesthésie, flux).
Vous avez par ailleurs l’opportunité de vous impliquer concrètement dans plusieurs projets à différents niveaux d’avancements ou de coordination.

Votre principale mission consiste à accueillir les familles de la patientèle durant les weekends et les jours fériés au Service des soins intensifs. 
Vous accompagnez les familles auprès de leurs proches tout en assurant le standard téléphonique durant leur présence.
Vous effectuez également certains travaux de secrétariat, triez et classez les dossiers de la patientèle pour la numérisation.

En regard de votre parcours de formation pour l’obtention de votre titre en psychiatrie et psychothérapie, vous intégrez une unité de soins du département et assurez, au sein d'une équipe pluridisciplinaire, le suivi psychiatrique et psychothérapeutique hospitalier ou ambulatoire des patientes et patients de votre unité.
Parallèlement à votre activité, vous bénéficiez d'une formation post-graduée clinique et structurée intégrée de qualité selon les exigences de la FMH pour l'obtention du titre de spécialiste en psychiatrie et psychothérapie.
Il vous est également possible de participer aux activités de recherches en cours au niveau des services. Vous pouvez également bénéficier d’un accompagnement pour effectuer une thèse de doctorat.
Une formation intégrée de qualité répondant aux exigences de la Fédération des médecins suisses (FMH) qui comprend tant une formation pratique par l’activité clinique que théorique dans l’ensemble des champs de la psychiatrie ainsi que dans les trois principaux axes de la psychothérapie.
Dans le cadre de votre formation, vous assurez un tournus au sein des différents services du département selon votre choix de parcours de formation.
A cette formation pratique et théorique se rajoute la participation à des supervisions de psychothérapie et des congrès. 
Le département prend en charge l’ensemble de la formation.

Dans le cadre de votre formation en infectiologie, vous intégrez le SPCI en vue de l’obtention du diplôme de formation approfondie en PCI, certifiée par l’ISFM. La formation porte en particulier sur l’épidémiologie, la microbiologie et plus particulièrement la résistance aux antibiotiques, l’hygiène environnementale, la désinfection/stérilisation et la gestion des risques et sciences comportementales (https://siwf.ch/files/pdf26/infektionspraevention_version_internet_f.pdf).
Au sein du SPCI, vous participez à des activités variées de consultation auprès des patients et patientes ainsi que des équipes professionnelles, logistiques et opérationnelles. Vous contribuez également aux activités de surveillance épidémiologique et des pratiques de soins, notamment par le suivi des micro-organismes multirésistants et des événements infectieux sporadiques, épidémiques ou endémiques associés aux soins. Le poste inclut en outre une participation aux activités de formation et d’enseignement, y compris la formation des nouveaux collaborateurs et collaboratrices des HUG et l’animation d’ateliers thématiques. Enfin, vous êtes associée ou associé aux activités de promotion et de recherche du SPCI. A ce titre, vous aurez l’occasion de participer aux études cliniques observationnelles et interventionnelles en cours au sein du service.
Dans le cadre de votre activité de base, vous êtes amené ou amenée à contribuer de manière significative au projet national de surveillance et prévention des bactériémies associées aux cathéters vasculaires centraux (CLABSI), en collaboration avec d’autres hôpitaux suisses et en particulier Swissnoso ainsi que l’Office Fédéral de la Santé Publique (OFSP). Cette activité inclut des taches de coordination, gestion d’équipe, recherche, communication et d’implémentation des modules de surveillance et prévention au niveau local et national.
Evoluant dans un environnement universitaire stimulant et exigeant, au sein d’une équipe pluridisciplinaire, vous participez à l’encadrement des stagiaires, étudiantes et étudiantes et doctorants. Vous êtes supervisé ou supervisée par le médecin chef et les médecins adjoints du service et vous collaborez de façon étroite avec l’équipe des ISC, les médecins ainsi que les collaborateurs et collaboratrices scientifiques.

At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position
The ML for Biosystems Engineering group led by Jonas Fleck at the Institute of Human Biology (IHB) in Basel, Switzerland is seeking a Postdoctoral Researcher to develop machine learning methods for organoid phenotyping and high-throughput screening. Join us to develop next-generation computational methods for drug discovery with complex human model systems.
 
The Opportunity

You will lead a research project developing computational methods to address important challenges in organoid engineering and drug discovery. Working in a highly collaborative environment with outstanding computational and experimental scientists, you'll develop state-of-the-art statistical and machine learning methods to tackle challenging questions in human biology and disease.
You'll have the chance to work with rich, high-content datasets from complex human model systems, such as large-scale perturbation experiments with multi-modal readouts. In collaboration with experimental scientists at IHB, you will also have the opportunity to shape future experiments, enabling you to develop methods with direct translational impact.
Possible research areas may include:
Causal inference and mechanism discovery from perturbation experiments
Predictive modeling and analysis for high-throughput screening
Computational methods for quantitative comparison of spatial, genomic, and other molecular profiles from organoid models with patient data.
Your work will connect computational innovation with experimental applications, contributing to the development of next-generation human model systems for drug discovery. You will publish your research, contribute open-source tools to the broader scientific community, and gain exposure to drug discovery and development while building your scientific independence as a computational researcher.

Who You are:

PhD in computational biology, computer science, machine learning, bioinformatics, or related technical fields.
Track record of conducting impactful independent research, demonstrated through publications, preprints, or substantial research software contributions.
Strong research experience in statistical or machine learning methods, ideally applied to genomics or other high-dimensional biological data.
Proficiency in Python and experience with modern ML and scientific computing frameworks such as JAX, PyTorch or TensorFlow.
Strong scientific programming and software engineering practices, including version control, testing, reproducible research workflows, and agentic development tools.
Creativity, scientific curiosity, and enthusiasm for developing computational methods that address challenging problems in biomedical research.
Ability and motivation to work closely with experimental scientists and contribute to collaborative, interdisciplinary projects.

Nice to have:
Experience applying machine learning to biomedical data, including genomics, imaging, spatial, or multimodal datasets.
Experience with perturbation experiments, causal inference, high-throughput screening, or predictive modeling.
Contributions to open-source software or scientific computing tools.
Experience working closely with experimental collaborators.

Technical details:

To be considered, your application needs a CV (including a list of relevant publications) and a cover letter describing your research interests.

About the Institute of Human Biology (IHB) & Basel:
The Institute of Human Biology (IHB) is a research center in Basel, Switzerland, dedicated to engineering advanced human model systems for drug discovery, development, and precision medicine. The IHB fosters an interdisciplinary environment bridging academic and pharmaceutical research, connecting biologists, engineers, and data scientists. It has close ties to Roche's Pharmaceutical Research and Early Development (pRED) organization and Genentech (gRED), and collaborates with leading academic institutions including ETH Zürich, University of Basel, and EPFL, as well as globally. Basel is an international hub for research and innovation, cultivating training environments through institutions like the University of Basel and ETH Zürich's Department of Biosystems Sciences and Engineering, creating a melting pot of research development and commercialization.

We are looking forward to your application!
 
 

Who we are
A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.

Let’s build a healthier future, together.

Roche is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

As part of the ATLAS Detector Cooling team, you will contribute to the qualification, integration, and commissioning of the 2PACL CO₂ cooling system supporting future detector upgrades. You will be involved in thermal testing, instrumentation and DAQ development, data analysis, and the installation and commissioning of cooling infrastructure, gaining unique experience in the deployment of complex systems for a world-leading scientific experiment.
Your responsibilities
Contribute to the testing and validation of detector structures and 2PACL CO₂ cooling system components, including comparison of experimental results with simulation models.
Participate in the design, construction, and operation of thermal test setups, instrumentation, and data acquisition (DAQ) systems.
Analyse and interpret test data to assess system performance and support detector integration activities.
Collaborate with detector teams by providing technical feedback and supporting detector integration and commissioning work.
Contribute to the installation, commissioning, and performance validation of the 2PACL cooling system, including cooling distribution lines and vacuum infrastructure.
Your profile
Initial experience in thermal-fluid systems, cooling technologies, or heat transfer gained through academic, research, or engineering projects.
Experience with simulation or modelling of thermal and fluid systems.
Experience using CAD software for 2D and/or 3D mechanical design (e.g. CATIA V5 or similar tools).
Hands-on experience with instrumentation, laboratory testing, or data acquisition (DAQ) systems.
Experience analysing and interpreting experimental or simulation data.
Skills
Good understanding of thermodynamics and heat transfer principles, ideally including exposure to two-phase cooling systems.
Knowledge of fluid mechanics and thermal-fluid system behaviour.
Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics and technical drawings.
Familiarity with instrumentation, sensor integration, and data acquisition (DAQ) systems.
Understanding of SCADA systems and industrial control environments.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Electromechanical Engineering, Refrigeration (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is either a Bachelor's or Master's degree.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.
Applicants without University degree are not eligible.
Applicants with a PhD are not eligible.

Dans le cadre des interventions par ultrasons focalisés pour traiter le tremblement chez les patientes et patients atteints de tremblement essentiel ou de la maladie de Parkinson, vous avez la charge de la partie technique pour les interventions, sous la supervision des neurochirurgiens.
Votre rôle consiste à préparer les interventions : calcul du SDR, tractographie des faisceaux, commande du matériel. Vous apportez un support pendant les interventions : calibration du système, acquisition et analyse de données (tremblement, voix).
Vous identifiez et résolvez les problèmes techniques et assurez un suivi des interventions dans un but d’amélioration constante (effets secondaires, paramètres de traitements, rapports d’incidents auprès du fabricant etc.).
